Discovery honestly reports 'No switches found' (log line 'Discovery complete for Switch: 0 devices, 0 backend errors'), and there is no way to instantiate a fake Switch from the UI, so the switch control card never renders. Evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-disc-bottom.png

The dialog is gated on selecting a Fujifilm camera. No Fujifilm driver or simulator is present (gPhoto2 detected 0 cameras, native discovery found 0 devices), so the disclaimer path is unreachable without hardware.

findings.title: Opening Edit Profile and pressing Save silently destroys the reducer and rewrites focal length / image scale by 25%
findings.what_happened: The onboarding wizard let me set telescope FL 550 mm, aperture 100 mm and a 0.80x reducer; it correctly computed and stored effective FL 440.0 mm, f/4.4, image scale 1.76 arcsec/px. Equipment > Edit Profile has NO reducer/barlow field at all -- its Optical Train section only has Telescope/OTA, Focal Length and Aperture, and it displayed 'f/5.5' and 'Scale 1.41"/px at 3.76um'. I changed nothing and clicked 'Save Changes'. The DB went from focal_length=440.0, focal_ratio=4.4 to focal_length=550.0, focal_ratio=5.5. The reducer is now unrecoverable: no field anywhere in Edit Profile accepts it (AT-SPI tree of the whole dialog contains no 'Reducer' or 'Barlow' node), so the only place it can ever be entered is the one-time first-run wizard.
findings.expected: Edit Profile should expose the reducer/barlow factor and preserve it, and the computed f/ratio and image scale should match what the profile actually stores (f/4.4, 1.76 arcsec/px). A no-op open+save must never mutate the profile.
findings.repro: 1. Complete onboarding with telescope library 'Sky-Watcher Esprit 100ED' (550mm/100mm), reducer 0.80, pixel size 3.76um. Review screen shows 'Focal length 550.0 mm x 0.80', 'Image scale 1.76 arcsec/px'. 2. sqlite3 <db> 'select focal_length,focal_ratio from equipment_profiles' -> 440.0 | 4.4. 3. Equipment > Edit Profile > scroll to Optical Train: shows f/5.5 and Scale 1.41"/px. 4. Click 'Save Changes' without editing anything. 5. Re-query: 550.0 | 5.5.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-optics2.png (wizard: 440.0 mm, f/4.40, 1.76 arcsec/px), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-30-review.png (summary: 550.0 mm x 0.80, 1.76 arcsec/px), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-ep2.png (Edit Profile: f/5.5, 1.41"/px, no reducer field); DB before/after captured in-session: focal_length 440.0->550.0, focal_ratio 4.4->5.5
findings.proposed_fix: Add a Reducer/Barlow factor field to the Edit Profile Optical Train section, seeded from the profile; compute effective focal length = telescope_focal_length * reducer and store that in focal_length exactly as the wizard does. Until then, at minimum make Edit Profile round-trip focal_length rather than recomputing it from telescope_focal_length. A 25% image-scale error breaks plate-solve scale hints, framing FOV and guider px->arcsec calibration.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live end-to-end. Seeded a wizard-shaped profile (focal_length=440.0, focal_ratio=4.4, telescope_focal_length=550.0, aperture=100.0), opened Equipment > Edit Profile (screenshot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-07-optical.png shows Focal Length 550.0, f/5.5, Scale 1.41"/px against a profile that stores 440.0/f4.4/1.76"/px), clicked Save Changes with zero edits, and re-queried: 550.0 | 100.0 | 5.5 | 550.0. Mechanism confirmed in code: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/onboarding_provider.dart:408-413 writes focalLength = focalLengthMm * reducerFactor but telescopeFocalLength = the RAW focalLengthMm; packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/equipment/dialogs/profile_editor_dialog.dart:209-212 seeds the Focal Length field from telescopeFocalLength in preference to focalLength; profile_editor_dialog/profile_data_operations.dart:517,546-548 then writes that same value back into BOTH focalLength and focalRatio. A grep for reducer/barlow across packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/equipment/ returns zero hits, so the reducer really is wizard-only. Severity corrected P0->P1: it is silent and corrupts plate-solve scale hints / FOV / guider px->arcsec, but it is not unrecoverable as claimed -- typing 440 into Focal Length round-trips correctly (both columns then hold 440); only the reducer as a separate concept is unrepresentable.

findings.title: INDI 'Test Connection' reports a green 'Connected' against a host that does not exist
findings.what_happened: Settings > Equipment > Connection > INDI Server Address > Configure > Test Connection returned a green tick and 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' with nothing listening on localhost:7624 (verified: ss shows no listener, /dev/tcp connect returns 'Connection refused', no indiserver process). I then changed the host to 192.0.2.77 (RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1, guaranteed unroutable) and pressed Test again: after a real ~30s attempt it again reported the green 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' The same app's PHD2 test on the very same screen correctly reports 'No response on localhost:4400. Is PHD2 running with "Enable Server" turned on?', so this is not a platform limitation.
findings.expected: 'Test Connection' must report failure when the TCP connect fails, e.g. 'No response on 192.0.2.77:7624'. Reporting success is worse than no test at all: a user with a Raspberry Pi INDI server who typos the address gets a green tick and then spends the night hunting the wrong problem.
findings.repro: 1. Ensure no indiserver is running. 2. Settings > Equipment > Connection > 'INDI Server Address' > Configure. 3. Click 'Test Connection' with localhost:7624 -> green 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' 4. Replace host with 192.0.2.77, click Test Connection -> same green success.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-indi2.png (localhost:7624 green 'Connected. Found 0 devices.'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-indi4.png (192.0.2.77 same green result); port verification: `ss -ltnp | grep 7624` empty, `/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/7624` -> Connection refused, `pgrep indiserver` empty
findings.proposed_fix: Treat a failed TCP connect / handshake timeout as failure and surface the socket error, mirroring the PHD2 test's wording. Distinguish 'connected, 0 devices' (server up, no drivers loaded) from 'could not reach host'.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live. Verified nothing was listening (ss -ltn | grep 7624 empty, pgrep indiserver empty, /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/7624 -> Connection refused), then Settings > Equipment > Connection > INDI Server Address > Configure > Test Connection returned the green tick 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-26-inditest.png). The reporter did not name the actual cause; I did: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/backend/ffi_backend/discovery_camera_operations.dart:86-102 (_discoverAddressDevices) wraps the bridge call in try/catch, logs a warning and returns const <DeviceInfo>[]. The Rust side is correct -- api_discover_indi_at_address (native/.../bridge/src/api/discovery.rs:153-168) maps the failure to SkotiqError::connection_failed and IndiClient::connect (native/.../indi/src/client.rs:780-794) returns ConnectionFailed on a refused socket -- so the dialog's own catch branch (indi_server_dialog.dart:129-137, 'Connection failed: $e') is simply unreachable. Severity P1 confirmed.

findings.title: Onboarding's 'Regulated cooling' toggle never enables cooling; the camera runs at ambient every session
findings.what_happened: Onboarding step 9 'Set your capture defaults' has a 'Regulated cooling' switch ('Turn on for a cooled camera; leave off for a DSLR or an uncooled sensor'). I turned it ON and it revealed 'Cooling set-point -10 C'. The saved profile has default_cooling_temp=-10.0 but cool_on_connect=0. On every connect the camera sat at 20.0 C with the cooler at 0%, and the app log shows it polling and doing nothing: '[CameraTemperaturePoller] Camera temp: 20.0C, power: 0%, target: -10.0C'. The connect sequence issues camera_set_gain and camera_set_offset but no cooling command at all. The manual 'Cool to -10C' button works (reaches -10.0 C / 35% within ~50 s), and ticking the hidden 'Cool on connect' checkbox inside Equipment > Edit Profile > Camera Defaults makes the camera cool automatically on the next Connect All -- so the feature works; only the wizard fails to wire it. There is also no cooling control anywhere in Settings: searching Settings for 'cool' returns 'No settings match your search', while app_settings holds cooling_behavior='On Connect' with no UI and no effect.
findings.expected: Turning on 'Regulated cooling' with a set-point in the wizard should set cool_on_connect=1 so the camera actually reaches the set-point when it connects. Otherwise the switch is decorative and a first-run user images all night on a warm sensor.
findings.repro: 1. Fresh profile, walk onboarding, step 9: turn 'Regulated cooling' ON, leave set-point -10. Save profile. 2. sqlite3 <db> 'select cool_on_connect,default_cooling_temp from equipment_profiles' -> 0 | -10.0. 3. Equipment > Connect All. Camera card shows 20.0 C / 0% / Idle indefinitely. 4. Equipment > Edit Profile > Camera Defaults > tick 'Cool on connect' > Save. 5. Disconnect All, Connect All -> camera card shows -10.0 C / 35%.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-cool.png (wizard toggle ON + set-point -10), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-camcard3.png (20.0C/0% after reconnect), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-ep5.png ('Cool on connect' unchecked in Edit Profile), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-cool4.png (-10.0C/35% after enabling it), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-searchcool.png ('No settings match your search' for 'cool'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/dumplog.txt line 'Camera temp: 20.0C, power: 0%, target: -10.0C'
findings.proposed_fix: Map the wizard's 'Regulated cooling' switch to cool_on_connect (and keep default_cooling_temp for the set-point). Also either surface or delete the orphaned app_settings key cooling_behavior='On Connect', which has no UI and no effect.
findings.verdict_reasoning: The factual core is confirmed in code but the finding's framing is over-called. packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/onboarding_provider.dart:429 hardcodes coolOnConnect: false, with an explicit 8-line comment stating this is deliberate ('we never auto-run the TEC on connect just because a set-point exists: a setup done in the middle of a summer day must not pin the cooler at full power for hours'). The wizard control (packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/onboarding/steps/camera_defaults_step.dart:359-361) is labelled 'Regulated cooling / Turn on for a cooled camera; leave off for a DSLR or an uncooled sensor' -- it is a camera-capability question, it never promises cool-on-connect, and it is not decorative: it gates and persists default_cooling_temp. So 'the toggle never enables cooling' is true only against an expectation the UI does not set. The orphan-setting sub-claim IS fully confirmed and is the real defect here: 'cooling_behavior' defaults to 'On Connect' (database/default_settings.dart:55), is round-tripped through every settings mapper, has zero consumers that act on it (grep across packages/ and apps/ excluding generated files finds only storage/mapping), and has no UI -- I reproduced 'No settings match your search' for 'cool' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-22-searchcool.png). Severity P1 -> P3.

findings.title: Sequence recovery checkpoint is stored at a hardcoded shared path, so a brand-new profile was offered another database's interrupted run -- and discarding it deleted that run's recovery data
findings.what_happened: On a --fresh profile whose database contains zero rows in sequences, sequence_runs and sequence_checkpoints, the app popped a modal 'Recover Sequence? A previous sequence was interrupted and can be resumed. Sequence: AUDIT SEQ, Saved 0m ago, Completed 16 frames (0m integration)' -- on top of the First Night Walkthrough of a first-run user. The checkpoint is written to ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint, ignoring SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR/SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR, and belongs to a different data directory entirely (its save_path is /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-run/captures). The modal has only Discard/Resume and Escape does not dismiss it, so to continue I had to press Discard -- which deleted both the checkpoint and its .bak, destroying the other instance's recovery state. Two further problems in the same file: the checkpoint says executor_state='Completed' and is_active=false while the dialog calls it 'interrupted'; and completed_exposures=16 with completed_integration_secs=0.0 for a 3.0 s x 20 node, which the UI renders as '16 frames (0m integration)'.
findings.expected: The recovery checkpoint must live under the active data directory so it can never describe a run that is not in the open database, the dialog must not offer to resume a run whose executor_state is Completed, and a fresh install must never see this modal.
findings.repro: 1. Run instance A against data dir X, start and interrupt a sequence named AUDIT SEQ. 2. Start instance B with SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=Y (empty DB). 3. B shows 'Recover Sequence? ... AUDIT SEQ'. 4. sqlite3 Y/skotiq.db 'select * from sequence_checkpoints' -> empty. 5. Press Discard in B -> ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint and .bak are both gone.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-32-firstnight.png (the modal on a fresh profile), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/checkpoint-evidence.json (the checkpoint: name 'AUDIT SEQ', save_path /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-run/captures, executor_state 'Completed', is_active false, completed_exposures 16, completed_integration_secs 0.0); my DB's sequences/sequence_runs/sequence_checkpoints all returned zero rows
findings.where: native checkpoint writer -> ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint (path resolution ignores SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR); recovery prompt raised from app_shell
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve the checkpoint path from the same data-dir resolver the database uses, stamp the owning database/profile id into the checkpoint and refuse to offer recovery when it does not match, and gate the prompt on executor_state != Completed.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Core mechanism independently reproduced LIVE, by accident, mid-verification. My equipment-shell-verify instance (SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/equipment-shell-verify/data, whose DB returned 0 rows from sequences, sequence_runs AND sequence_checkpoints) was shown 'Recover Sequence? A previous sequence was interrupted... Sequence: New Sequence' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-46-flerror2.png). The checkpoint at ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint had save_path /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-nodes/captures -- a concurrently running agent's data dir. Escape did not dismiss it (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-47-esc.png). Relaunching with XDG_DATA_HOME redirected into my scratch dir made the prompt vanish, proving the path is XDG/getApplicationSupportDirectory-derived (app_shell.dart:347-348) and ignores SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR, which the rest of native persistence does honour (e.g. calibration_handlers.dart:110). Discard is destructive as claimed: CheckpointManager::clear() (native/.../sequencer/src/checkpoint.rs:746-757) removes both the primary and the .bak. HOWEVER one sub-claim is REFUTED: the dialog cannot have been raised from a checkpoint whose executor_state is 'Completed' and is_active false. can_resume() (checkpoint.rs:481-492) requires is_active && state in {Running, Paused}, and app_shell returns noRecovery when !canResume. My live capture showed executor_state=Paused, is_active=true. The reporter's checkpoint-evidence.json is a LATER snapshot -- mark_completed() (checkpoint.rs:765-771) rewrites exactly those two fields when the other instance's run finished. Severity P1 -> P2: on a real single install there is one support dir and one DB, so cross-database contamination requires an explicit SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR override; the genuine defect is the resolver disagreeing with the rest of native persistence plus a cross-instance-destructive Discard.

findings.title: First Light 'Submit' button is a dead control -- the advertised TNS/AAVSO submission does nothing
findings.what_happened: Analytics > Science > First Light shows a candidate card whose own header text says 'Anything that appeared, moved, or brightened on a deep patch lands here to review, then submit to the TNS or export an AAVSO / MPC report.' The card's primary (filled, full-width) 'Submit' button does nothing: 4 clicks across both the Unnamed and Confirmed states produced no dialog, no snackbar, no log entry and no DB change. The AT-SPI tree after clicking contains no dialog node. The coordinate is correct: the sibling 'Confirm' button on the same row at the same y works (transient_detections.reviewed went 0 -> 1 and the badge changed to 'Confirmed'), and 'Chase' opens a 'Chase this candidate?' dialog.
findings.expected: Submit should open the transient submit dialog (transient_submit_dialog.dart exists and is the only consumer of that flow), or be disabled with an explanation if submission is not configured.
findings.repro: 1. Have at least one row in transient_detections. 2. Analytics > Science > First Light. 3. Click 'Submit' on the candidate card -- nothing happens. 4. Click 'Confirm' on the same row -- badge flips to Confirmed and reviewed=1 in the DB. 5. Click 'Submit' again on the now-Confirmed card -- still nothing.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-106-fl3.png (card with Submit/Confirm/Chase), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-flcard2.png (after Confirm worked), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-111-submit2.png (unchanged after Submit on a Confirmed card); AT-SPI tree grep for tns/reporter/discovery-report returned only the panel description text
findings.proposed_fix: Wire Submit to show TransientSubmitDialog. If submission requires credentials that are unset, disable the button and say so rather than rendering it as the primary action.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Submit is fully wired and gives explicit feedback in every state; I drove all three. (1) Unreviewed candidate: Submit showed the snackbar 'Not yet confirmed - mark this detection as confirmed before submitting.' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-15-submit-unreviewed.png). (2) After Confirm (DB reviewed 0->1): Submit opened the full 'Submit discovery' dialog with AAVSO / MPC / TNS network chips, a Preview button and 'Submit to TNS' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-17-submitdlg.png). (3) On a dipole candidate: 'Dipole artefacts are not real transients - they cannot be submitted.' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-19-dipolesubmit.png). Code matches: transient_candidate_card.dart:380-409, canSubmit = detection.reviewed && !isDipole, with a handler on BOTH branches. The reporter's own evidence identifies their row as a dipole: the alert popover type 'Other' is produced only by _typeForKind(TransientKind.dipole) (transient_alert_mapper.dart:58-59), and TransientKind.fromWire falls back to dipole for any unrecognised token (transient_candidate.dart:42-50). So the button was correctly refusing to push an artefact to the TNS. They likely missed the bottom-edge snackbar, which is what the AT-SPI 'no dialog node' check would not catch.

findings.title: Equipment readiness panel omits the mount entirely when it is disconnected
findings.what_happened: With all four profile devices (camera, mount, focuser, filter wheel) disconnected, the STATUS panel listed only two device items: 'Critical devices - Camera is not connected' and 'Profile devices - Assigned in your profile but not connected: Focuser, Filter Wheel. They will be unavailable this session.' The mount is not mentioned in either item, or anywhere else on the screen. A user scanning the readiness list before heading out would conclude the mount is fine.
findings.expected: Every profile device that is not connected must appear in the readiness list, and a disconnected mount should be a blocking/critical item -- it is the one failure that ends a night outright.
findings.repro: 1. Profile with camera, mount, focuser and filter wheel assigned. 2. Equipment > Disconnect All. 3. Read the STATUS panel: only Camera (critical) and 'Focuser, Filter Wheel' (profile devices) are listed.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-readiness-mount.png, full context /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-80-coolonconnect.png (main area reads 'No devices connected', pill 0/4)
findings.proposed_fix: Build the 'Profile devices' list from every assigned-but-unconnected device including the mount, and promote mount to the critical tier alongside camera.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Behaviour reproduced: with all four profile devices disconnected I opened the full 'Ready to image' dialog (View all) and it lists exactly two device items -- 'Critical devices: Camera is not connected' and 'Profile devices: Assigned in your profile but not connected: Focuser, Filter Wheel' -- with the mount named nowhere (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-10-viewall.png). Cause: readiness_provider.dart:105-112 deliberately filters camera and mount OUT of offlineProfileDevices ('already covered by the critical-devices item'), while _buildCriticalDevices (readiness_models.dart:310-357) reports only the single highest-priority fault, so the mount branch is masked whenever the camera is also down. Two parts of the finding are overstated: the mount IS already in the critical tier (it surfaces as 'Mount is not connected - you can capture but cannot slew or track' the instant the camera connects, so 'promote mount to the critical tier' is a no-op), and it is not absent 'anywhere else on the screen' -- the profile card shows 0/4 with per-device dots and the status bar reads 'Mount Disconnected'. Severity P1 -> P2.

findings.title: 'Connect All result' strip keeps claiming devices are Connected after they have been disconnected
findings.what_happened: After Connect All, a persistent strip sits under the header reading 'Connect All result | camera Connected | mount Connected | focuser Connected | filter wheel Connected | Clear'. I then disconnected the camera: its card vanished, the header pill correctly changed to '3 connected' and the status bar to '3/4 | Camera Disconnected' -- but the strip still showed a green 'camera Connected'. Worse, after Disconnect All the strip still showed all four green 'Connected' chips while the main area said 'No devices connected' and the pill said 0/4. On the next launch the same strip is relabelled 'Startup auto-connect result' and behaves the same way.
findings.expected: Either clear/update the strip when connection state changes, or label it unambiguously as a historical record with a timestamp ('Connect All at 11:16: 4 of 4 succeeded') so a green 'Connected' chip is never read as current state.
findings.repro: 1. Equipment > Connect All (strip appears, 4 green chips). 2. Click the disconnect icon on the camera card > 'Disconnect anyway'. 3. Strip still shows 'camera Connected' while the pill reads '3 connected'. 4. Disconnect All -> strip still shows all four Connected next to 'No devices connected'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-camdisc.png (camera card gone, strip still 'camera Connected'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-80-coolonconnect.png ('No devices connected' + 0/4 with four green Connected chips), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-pill.png ('3 connected'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-sb2.png ('3/4 Camera Disconnected')
findings.proposed_fix: Re-render the strip from live device state, or freeze it as a timestamped result banner that visually cannot be confused with the live status chips.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly: after Disconnect All the strip still showed four green chips 'camera/mount/focuser/filter wheel Connected' while the main area read 'No devices connected' and the profile card read 0/4 (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-09-disc.png); on the next launch the same strip was relabelled 'Startup auto-connect result' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-35-equip3.png). This is by design and documented: equipment_screen/progress_dashboard.dart:10-14 -- 'After a sweep completes the chips remain visible until clear() is called, so the user can review what failed without having to re-run Connect All' -- and the widget renders purely from the deviceConnectionProgressProvider snapshot with no live device state. Severity P2 -> P3: the strip is already labelled with a past-tense '<source> result' and carries a Clear button, and the live pill/status bar/profile card all disagree with it visibly on the same screen; the real gap is the missing timestamp and the identical chip styling.

findings.title: Red night theme renders full-saturation blue, cyan and green accent swatches
findings.what_happened: Settings > Appearance > Theme > 'Red night' correctly re-tints the whole shell, nav rail, cards and status bar in red. The 'Accent color' swatch row directly underneath it, however, stays fully saturated. Sampling the rendered pixels: (91,158,196) blue, (16,185,129) green, (245,158,11) amber, (239,68,68) red, (40,120,168) blue, (236,72,153) pink, (6,182,212) cyan. Cyan and green at those levels are exactly the short-wavelength, high-luminance content red-night mode exists to eliminate.
findings.expected: In red night mode every pixel should be red-channel-dominant. Either desaturate the accent swatches to red-luminance stand-ins (with the name as the differentiator) or hide the accent picker in red night with a note that accent colour does not apply.
findings.repro: 1. Settings > Appearance > Theme = Red night. 2. Look at the Accent color row on the same page. 3. Sample the swatch pixels.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-62-rednight.png (whole page red, swatches not), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-dd3.png (close-up with the Red night dropdown open); pixel samples at y=443: x=1524 (91,158,196), x=1553 (16,185,129), x=1698 (6,182,212)
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/... appearance accent-colour row (swatches bypass the red-night colour filter)
findings.proposed_fix: Route the accent swatches through the same red-night transform as the rest of the theme, or replace them with labelled red-tinted chips while red night is active.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced and re-measured independently at full resolution. With Theme = Red night the whole shell is red (sampled surfaces: nav rail (0,0,0), card (20,8,8)) but the Accent color row is untouched: (91,158,196), (16,185,129), (245,158,11), (239,68,68), (40,120,168), (236,72,153), (6,182,212) -- the exact values the reporter cited. Evidence /tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-30-rednight.png and eqv-29-rednight-raw.png. The green and cyan are precisely the short-wavelength high-luminance content red-night mode exists to remove. Severity P2 stands.

findings.title: Window minimize / maximize / close disappear below ~800px window width, leaving no way to close the app
findings.what_happened: The desktop build draws its own title bar (no OS decorations). At 1600x900 and at 900x750 the bar carries remote-status, notifications, account, settings, minimize, maximize and close. Resizing the window to 760x700 switches the shell to the mobile layout (bottom navigation bar: Home/Gear/Imaging/Sequence/Guiding/Plan/More) and the title bar collapses to just the wordmark and a single settings gear -- minimize, maximize and close are gone, along with the notifications and account buttons. With no OS decorations there is then no mouse-reachable way to close or minimize the window.
findings.expected: Window controls belong to the desktop window regardless of width; the responsive breakpoint should never strip them. If the mobile shell is deliberately reused below the breakpoint, it must still render the platform window controls on desktop.
findings.repro: 1. Launch the Linux desktop build. 2. Resize the window to 760x700 (xdotool windowsize <win> 760 700). 3. Inspect the top bar: only the SKOTIQ wordmark and a gear remain.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-vnarrow-title.png (760px title bar), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-narrow.png (900px title bar with all controls), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-vnarrow.png (bottom nav bar appears)
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the desktop title-bar window controls in every layout on desktop platforms; gate only the label density on width.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced: xdotool windowsize 760 700 on the Linux release bundle switched the shell to the mobile layout (bottom nav Home/Gear/Imaging/Sequence/Guiding/Plan/More) and the title bar collapsed to the SKOTIQ wordmark plus a single settings gear -- minimize, maximize, close, notifications and account all gone (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-32-narrow-crop.png). That bar is _MobileSettingsBar (app_shell.dart:865-916), which renders no window controls at all. The finding's premise that there are no OS decorations to fall back on also holds on Linux: apps/desktop/lib/main.dart:161 sets titleBarStyle: TitleBarStyle.hidden and window_manager's Linux plugin implements that as gtk_window_set_decorated(false). Minor overstatement: Alt+F4 and WM keyboard/menu paths still close the window, and widening past the breakpoint restores the controls, so 'no way to close the app' should read 'no mouse-reachable window control'. Severity P2 stands.

findings.title: The 'Deleted <profile>' snackbar never auto-dismisses and covers the entire status bar
findings.what_happened: Deleting an equipment profile raises a full-width bottom snackbar 'Deleted "My First Rig"  [Undo]'. It was still on screen 7 minutes later (delete confirmed at 11:36:45, snackbar still present in the AT-SPI tree at 11:43:29), it survived navigating from Equipment to Settings to Dashboard, it has no close button, and clicking elsewhere does not dismiss it. While it is up, the whole status bar -- profile name, device connection states, focuser position, temperature, clock and LST -- is hidden. Only restarting the app cleared it.
findings.expected: An undo snackbar should auto-dismiss after a few seconds (or on navigation), and should not permanently occlude the status bar.
findings.repro: 1. Equipment > right-click a profile > Delete > Delete. 2. Snackbar appears over the status bar. 3. Navigate to Settings and then Dashboard, wait several minutes -- it is still there.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-95-share.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-96-snackbar.png (snackbar over the status bar on two different screens); AT-SPI tree at 11:43:29 still contains 'Deleted "My First Rig"' + Undo button, delete performed 11:36:45
findings.proposed_fix: Give the snackbar a finite duration (e.g. 6 s), make it floating rather than full-width so it does not sit on the status bar, and add a dismiss affordance.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Behaviour reproduced precisely -- deleted a profile at 12:28:32, the snackbar 'Deleted "My First Rig" [Undo]' was still on screen at 12:30:04 (92 s) after navigating Equipment -> Dashboard, covering the entire status bar with no close affordance (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-40-snackbar.png, eqv-43-snacklate.png). BUT the diagnosis and the proposed fix are wrong and would change nothing: equipment_screen.dart:439 ALREADY sets duration: const Duration(seconds: 6). The real cause is a Flutter 3.44 framework default -- SnackBar's constructor sets persist = persist ?? action != null (flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/material/snack_bar.dart:303), and ScaffoldMessengerState's timer callback returns early without hiding when snackBar.persist is true (scaffold.dart:618-622). So EVERY snackbar in this app that carries an action never times out, which makes this a systemic issue, not a profile-delete one. Correct fix is persist: false (or showCloseIcon), not a duration. Severity P2 stands but the scope is wider than reported.

findings.title: First Light 'Retry' button never re-runs the query
findings.what_happened: The First Light candidate list failed to load and rendered 'Could not load candidates / FormatException: Invalid radix-10 number (at character 1) / tile-1 / ^' with a 'Retry' button. I corrected the underlying row in the database, then clicked Retry three times over several minutes: the identical error re-rendered every time, still quoting the old value 'tile-1' that no longer exists in the database. Restarting the app made the list load correctly and render the candidate, proving the data was fine and Retry simply never re-executed the query. Separately, this error state leaks a raw Dart exception (class name and caret diagram) straight into the user-facing UI.
findings.expected: Retry must invalidate and re-run the provider. The error surface should show a human message plus a copyable detail, not a raw FormatException with a caret.
findings.repro: 1. Put a row in transient_detections whose tile_id cannot be parsed as an int. 2. Analytics > Science > First Light -> error state. 3. Fix the row in the DB. 4. Click Retry repeatedly -> same error, same stale value. 5. Restart the app -> loads fine.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-104-firstlight.png (error), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-105-fl2.png (identical after DB fix + Retry), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-106-fl3.png (loads after restart with the same data)
findings.proposed_fix: Have Retry call ref.invalidate on the candidates provider. Wrap the error in a user-facing message and keep the exception behind a 'details' expander.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Symptom reproduced exactly: seeded transient_detections.tile_id = 'tile-1' (TEXT), First Light rendered 'Could not load candidates / FormatException: Invalid radix-10 number (at character 1) / tile-1 / ^' with the raw Dart exception and caret leaking into the UI; I then corrected the row to 7 and clicked Retry three times -- identical error, still quoting 'tile-1' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-49-flerror2.png, eqv-51-retry3.png). BUT the stated cause is wrong and the proposed fix is already in the code: first_light_view.dart:409 is literally onPressed: () => ref.invalidate(firstLightCandidatesProvider). The actual mechanism is that firstLightCandidatesProvider (transient_detections_provider.dart:138-150) is a StreamProvider over a drift select().watch() (transient_detections_dao.dart:73-78); drift's cached query stream replays its last snapshot -- here an error -- to the new subscriber instead of re-executing, so invalidate cannot clear it. Important caveat that halves the severity: both my repro and the reporter's corrected the row with an out-of-band sqlite3 write, which drift by design cannot observe; an in-app (drift) write to that table would push a fresh snapshot and recover the view. Severity P2 -> P3. The raw-exception-in-UI sub-claim is fully confirmed and is the part worth fixing outright.

findings.title: Diagnostic dump is described as 'recent log files' but bundles 7 days of logs from every Skotiq instance on the machine
findings.what_happened: Settings > Help & Tutorials > Generate Diagnostic Dump promises 'Recent log files -- logs/exported_logs.txt -- rotated native logs + in-app entries'. The produced zip contained a 4.78 MB, 38,299-line exported_logs.txt spanning 2026-07-26 through 2026-08-01, and 421 of its lines reference /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-run -- a completely different profile's capture directory, including that run's target names and FITS filenames. The native log is written to the hardcoded ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/logs/ regardless of SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR, so the dump is not scoped to the session or the data directory the user is running. The save dialog also defaults to the application's own bundle directory (apps/desktop/build/linux/x64/release/bundle), which in a real install is typically read-only.
findings.expected: 'Recent log files' should mean the current session (or a bounded window), scoped to the running data directory; and the save dialog should default to a writable user location such as Downloads or the configured capture folder.
findings.repro: 1. Settings > Help & Tutorials > Generate Diagnostic Dump > Open > Create dump. 2. Note the save dialog opens inside the app bundle directory. 3. Save and inspect: unzip -p dump.zip logs/exported_logs.txt | grep -c . -> 38299 lines, dates 2026-07-26..2026-08-01, and grep for other profiles' paths.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-72-dump.png (the 'Recent log files' claim), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-73-dump2.png (save dialog defaulting into the bundle dir), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/diagdump.zip and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/dumplog.txt (7 days, 421 lines referencing /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-run)
findings.proposed_fix: Bound the log export to the current session or last N hours, resolve the log directory from the active data dir, state the actual span in the UI, and default the save location to the user's Downloads/capture folder.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Every element verified. (a) The 'Recent log files / logs/exported_logs.txt' copy is at diagnostic_dump_screen.dart:194-195. (b) It is produced by LoggingService.exportLogs (logging_service.dart:378-410), which concatenates EVERY file returned by getLogFiles (336-365 -- all files in the log dir whose path contains 'skotiq.log') with no time bound whatsoever. (c) The log dir is getApplicationSupportDirectory()/logs (desktop_logging_init.dart:61-68), independent of SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR -- confirmed on disk: ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/logs holds 7 daily rotations 2026-07-26..2026-08-01 totalling 4.9 MB, and today's file was being written by MY scratch instance (SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/equipment-shell-verify/data) while I ran it. (d) Cross-instance leakage measured directly: today's shared log contains 454 lines referencing three other audit profiles' capture directories (/tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-run, /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-nodes, /tmp/ns-audit/equipment-shell). (e) The save-dialog claim holds: diagnostic_dump_screen.dart:132-140 calls chooseExportTarget with no initialDirectory and export_target.dart:74-78 passes that null straight to file_selector.getSaveLocation, so the picker opens at the process CWD. Severity P2 stands.

findings.title: The delete-profile confirmation says 'This cannot be undone' and then offers a working Undo
findings.what_happened: Right-click a profile > Delete raises 'Delete Profile / Delete "My First Rig"? This cannot be undone.' Confirming produces a snackbar with an Undo action, and Undo genuinely restores the profile in full: after undoing the deletion of my only profile the row came back with name, focal_length 550.0, filter_names ["LumTest","R","G","B","Ha","OIII","SII"], default_gain 100, cool_on_connect 1, is_default 1, is_active 1.
findings.expected: Say what is true: either drop the 'cannot be undone' sentence and mention the undo window, or remove the Undo.
findings.repro: 1. Equipment > right-click profile > Delete. 2. Read 'This cannot be undone.' 3. Confirm. 4. Click Undo in the snackbar. 5. sqlite3 <db> 'select * from equipment_profiles' -> profile fully restored.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-delconf.png ('This cannot be undone.'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-118-noprofiles2.png (Undo snackbar), post-undo DB row shown above
findings.proposed_fix: Change the copy to 'Delete "<name>"? You can undo this for a few seconds.'
findings.verdict_reasoning: Copy verified verbatim at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/equipment/widgets/profile_sidebar.dart:432 ('Delete "${profile.name}"? This cannot be undone.') and live (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-39-delconf.png), and confirming raises a snackbar carrying an Undo SnackBarAction (equipment_screen.dart:437-457) wired to _restoreDeletedProfile with a full versioned JSON export taken before the delete. One correction that makes it worse, not better, than reported: in my run the Undo did NOT restore -- I had navigated Equipment -> Dashboard first, and _restoreDeletedProfile is a State method guarded by mounted/_isCurrentProfileOperation, so it aborted silently with no feedback and the row stayed deleted. So the dialog says 'cannot be undone', then offers an Undo, and that Undo is silently unreliable once you leave the screen. Severity P3 stands for the copy defect.

findings.title: Two profiles can share the same name, making the delete confirmation genuinely ambiguous
findings.what_happened: The New Profile dialog validates an empty name ('Fix 1 problem before saving - Profile name is required') but accepts a name identical to an existing profile. I created a second profile also called 'My First Rig'; the sidebar then showed two entries distinguishable only by their subtitle ('Sky-Watcher Esprit 100ED + Sim...' vs '0 devices'), the screen header, the status bar and the Delete confirmation all just say 'My First Rig'. The delete dialog reading 'Delete "My First Rig"? This cannot be undone.' cannot tell the user which of the two is about to be destroyed. The second profile also saved with no devices and focal_length 0.0 with no warning.
findings.expected: Reject or auto-suffix duplicate profile names, and include a disambiguator (devices/telescope) in the delete confirmation.
findings.repro: 1. Equipment > '+' > name it exactly the same as an existing profile > Save Changes. 2. sqlite3 <db> 'select id,name from equipment_profiles' -> two rows, same name. 3. Right-click either > Delete: the dialog quotes only the shared name.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-84-dupname.png (two identical entries), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-del.png (ambiguous confirmation), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-emptyname.png (empty-name validation that does work)
findings.proposed_fix: Add a uniqueness check to the same validator that already catches the empty name, or append ' (2)'.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced: created a second profile named exactly 'My First Rig'; the DB now holds id 1 and id 2 with identical names (second saved with focal_length 0.0 and no devices, no warning), the sidebar shows two entries distinguishable only by subtitle ('Sky-Watcher Esprit 100ED + Sim...' vs '0 devices') (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-37-dupname.png), and the delete dialog quotes only 'Delete "My First Rig"? This cannot be undone.' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-39-delconf.png). Code confirms the gap: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/equipment_profile_validation.dart:95 is the only name check and it rejects nothing but empty; there is no uniqueness constraint on equipment_profiles.name (only a non-unique idx_profiles_name index). Severity P3 stands.

findings.title: Transient alert popover reports a -2.35 delta-mag brightening as 'mag 2.4'
findings.what_happened: A detection with delta_mag = -2.35 (a 2.35-magnitude brightening) renders in the title-bar notification popover as 'NS J0.71+41.3 / Other / mag 2.4 / NEW'. The candidate card itself correctly shows '-2.35 mag' with an up-arrow, so the two surfaces disagree. 'mag 2.4' reads as an apparent magnitude of 2.4 -- a naked-eye star -- not as a delta. The designation 'NS J0.71+41.3' also encodes RA in hours rather than the IAU JHHMMSS.s+DDMMSS form the TNS expects, for a feature whose stated purpose is TNS submission.
findings.expected: Show the signed delta with its symbol, e.g. 'delta-mag -2.35', matching the card. Use an IAU-form designation (this object is J004244.30+411607.3).
findings.repro: 1. Have a transient_detections row with delta_mag = -2.35, ra_deg 10.6847, dec_deg 41.2687. 2. Click the bell in the title bar. 3. Popover reads 'NS J0.71+41.3 ... mag 2.4'. 4. Compare with the card in Analytics > Science > First Light, which reads '-2.35 mag'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-119-bell.png (popover 'mag 2.4'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-106-fl3.png (card '-2.35 mag'); the card's RA/Dec formatting is correct (00h 42m 44.3s +41 16' 7.3")
findings.where: transient alert popover formatter and the designation builder feeding it
findings.proposed_fix: Format delta magnitudes with sign and a delta label everywhere, and build designations from the sexagesimal RA/Dec the card already computes correctly.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with the reporter's exact numbers. Seeded delta_mag = -2.35 at ra_deg 10.6847 / dec_deg 41.2687; the bell popover reads 'NS J0.71+41.3 / Other / mag 2.4 / NEW' while the First Light card for the same row reads '-2.35 mag' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-20-bell.png vs eqv-18-dipole.png). A second seeded row (-1.72) renders 'NS J13.50+47.2 ... mag 1.7'. Code: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/transients/transient_alert_mapper.dart:20 sets magnitude = detection.deltaMag?.abs() (sign discarded, then rendered under an apparent-magnitude label), and _provisionalName (62-68) builds 'NS J' + RA in HOURS to 2dp + sign + |dec| in degrees to 1dp -- not the IAU JHHMMSS.s+DDMMSS form the TNS expects, even though the card computes the correct sexagesimal (00h 42m 44.3s +41 16' 7.3"). Severity P3 stands.

findings.title: 'Connect All' silently connects a safety monitor that is not in the profile, and did not do so on an identical earlier click
findings.what_happened: The 'Connect All' button lives under the profile card in the profile sidebar, so it reads as 'connect this profile's devices'. The first press (15:11:28 UTC) connected exactly the four profile devices. A second, identical press five minutes later (15:16:32) connected the same four plus sim_safety_monitor_1, which is not assigned to the profile -- the header pill changed to '5 connected - 1 unsaved' while the profile card and status bar both still said 4/4. The only thing that changed in between was that I had expanded the Discovery panel, which re-ran discovery. The device card does carry an honest note ('This session only -- not saved to your profile, so it will not reconnect next launch. Use Assign in Discovery to keep it.'), but the same button producing different results on two identical presses is the problem.
findings.expected: Connect All should have one defined scope. If it deliberately picks up safety monitors, do it consistently and label the button accordingly ('Connect profile + safety'); otherwise restrict it to the profile.
findings.repro: 1. Equipment > Connect All (log shows 4 connects). 2. Expand the Discovery panel (discovery re-runs). 3. Disconnect All, then Connect All again -> the log now also shows 'Connecting to Safety Monitor device: sim_safety_monitor_1' and the pill reads '5 connected - 1 unsaved'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-63-rednight-eq.png (safety monitor card + '5 connected - 1 unsaved' with profile still 4/4); app log 15:11:28 connects camera/focuser/mount/filterwheel only, 15:16:32 connects those four plus sim_safety_monitor_1
findings.proposed_fix: Make the connect-all set deterministic from the profile (plus an explicit, documented safety-device rule) rather than from whatever the last discovery happened to cache.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced: Connect All on a 4-device profile produced the pill '5 connected - 1 unsaved' with the profile card still 4/4 and a Simulated Safety Monitor card carrying the 'This session only - not saved to your profile' note (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-11-connectall.png); the app log shows 'Connecting to Safety Monitor device: sim_safety_monitor_1'. Cause found (the finding's file path is wrong -- there is no screens/equipment/command_handlers.dart): packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/equipment/equipment_screen.dart:659-700, immediately after the profile sweep, best-efforts a connect to unifiedSafetyMonitorsProvider.first when no safety monitor is connected. Because that provider is fed by the discovery cache, the outcome genuinely differs between two identical presses depending on whether discovery has run -- which is exactly the non-determinism reported. The profile sweep itself (device_service/profile_connections.dart:146-180) is correctly profile-scoped. Severity P3 stands.

findings.title: The onboarding wizard's filter step lets you invent slots the wheel does not have
findings.what_happened: After selecting the Simulated Filter Wheel the step listed its real 7 slots (L, R, G, B, Ha, OIII, SII). Pressing 'Add slot' immediately created an 8th row pre-filled 'Filter 8' with no warning that the connected wheel only reports 7 positions. Deleting a slot is also unconfirmed and renumbers everything below it, which would silently re-map per-filter focus offsets.
findings.expected: Cap the slot count at what the wheel reports (or warn clearly that slot 8 does not exist on this wheel), and warn that deleting a middle slot renumbers the ones below it.
findings.repro: 1. Onboarding step 6, select the Simulated Filter Wheel (7 slots appear). 2. Click 'Add slot' -> row 8 'Filter 8' appears with no warning.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-fw2.png (8 rows on a 7-position wheel), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-fw.png (the wheel's real 7 slots)
findings.proposed_fix: Disable 'Add slot' once the list reaches the wheel's reported position count, with a tooltip naming the count.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Confirmed by reading the named file; not driven live because re-entering onboarding would have wiped the profile the other verifications depend on. packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/onboarding/steps/filter_wheel_step.dart:268-275: onPressed: (_loadingSlots || _controllers.length >= 12) ? null : _addSlot -- the only cap is a hardcoded 12, never the wheel's reported position count, even though _seedSlotsFromDevice has just read that count from the device ('so the editor reflects the hardware (e.g. 8 slots), not a hardcoded default'). So on a 7-position wheel the button stays enabled and creates rows 8..12. The renumbering sub-claim also holds structurally: slot labels are '${i + 1}' from List.generate(_controllers.length, ...) (lines 282-295), so deleting a middle slot shifts every label below it, which silently re-maps per-filter focus offsets. Severity P3 stands.

findings.title: Three separate tutorial systems fire at once on a first run, and the second one tells the user to do what they just did
findings.what_happened: Finishing the 13-step onboarding wizard and choosing 'Take the first-night walkthrough' opens a 7-step modal wizard. Its 'Show me on the Sequencer screen' deep-link navigates correctly, but on arrival two more tutorials appear simultaneously: a coach-mark tour 'Step 1 of 7 - Welcome to Skotiq / Skotiq is your imaging assistant. Three things to set up first: equipment, a profile, and a sequence.' plus a bottom-right toast 'Sequencer Tour - Learn how to create and run automated imaging sequences. [Maybe Later] [Start Tour]'. The coach-mark tour's copy tells the user to set up equipment and a profile, which the 13-step wizard they just completed already did. Every screen then has its own persistent tour toast (Dashboard Tour, Equipment Tour, Imaging Tour, Settings Tour, Analytics Tour) that stays until individually dismissed and occludes the bottom-right of the content area.
findings.expected: One onboarding path at a time. The coach-mark tour should either not fire when a profile already exists, or be reworded to reflect completed state. Per-screen tour toasts should be suppressed while any other guided flow is active, and should be dismissible once globally.
findings.repro: 1. Fresh profile, complete onboarding, click 'Take the first-night walkthrough'. 2. Advance to step 7, click 'Show me on the Sequencer screen'. 3. Observe the Welcome coach-mark tour and the Sequencer Tour toast both appear.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-36-deeplink.png (walkthrough dismissed, Welcome tour + Sequencer Tour toast both up), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-37-tour2.png (coach-mark over the nav rail with the toast still present), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-narrow.png (Settings Tour toast covering settings rows at 900px)
findings.proposed_fix: Introduce a single 'guided flow active' flag; suppress the coach-mark tour and all per-screen toasts while a wizard is open, and skip the 'set up equipment and a profile' steps when a profile already exists.

findings.title: The onboarding step list marks a step complete just for visiting it
findings.what_happened: On the guider step I ran 'Test' against PHD2 with nothing listening; it correctly reported 'No response on localhost:4400...' and I selected no native guider. Pressing Next still put a filled blue tick next to 'Guider' in the left step list, identical to the ticks on Camera and Mount which really were configured. The Review screen is honest ('Guider - not set -'), so only the step list is misleading. Step 1's 'Back' button is also rendered enabled and is a silent no-op.
findings.expected: Tick a step only when it produced a value; show visited-but-skipped steps in a distinct state. Disable Back on step 1.
findings.repro: 1. Onboarding step 7, click 'Test' (fails), select nothing, click Next. 2. Sidebar shows 'Guider' with a filled tick. 3. Continue to step 12 -- Review says 'Guider - not set -'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-phd2.png (test correctly fails), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-15-opticaltrain.png (Guider ticked in the sidebar), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-30-review.png ('Guider - not set -')
findings.proposed_fix: Track per-step 'has value' separately from 'visited' and render skipped optional steps with a dash rather than a tick.

findings.title: Switching the active profile is only possible by changing which profile launches at startup
findings.what_happened: Clicking a non-active profile in the sidebar only highlights it -- the header, the connected devices and the status bar all stay on the previous profile, and the sidebar's footer collapses to just 'Edit Profile'. There is no 'Activate' / 'Use this profile' control anywhere. The only way I found to switch was right-click > 'Set as Default', which does switch is_active but also permanently changes what loads at startup. Profile management (Set as Default, Edit Profile, Duplicate, Delete) is entirely behind right-click; the profile card carries no overflow button or any other affordance advertising that a menu exists.
findings.expected: A visible primary action to switch the active profile for this session, kept separate from 'set as startup default', plus a visible '...' overflow on each profile card exposing the same menu that right-click does.
findings.repro: 1. Create two profiles. 2. Click the non-active one in the sidebar -- header and devices do not change; footer shows only 'Edit Profile'. 3. Right-click it -> the only way to make it active is 'Set as Default'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-85-switchprof.png (selected but not activated; footer has only Edit Profile), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-rclick.png (hidden context menu), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-setdef.png (Set as Default also switched is_active and flagged all five devices 'unsaved')
findings.proposed_fix: Add an 'Activate' button to the selected profile card and a '...' overflow menu; keep the star strictly for 'launch with this profile'.

findings.title: The optical-train step asks the user to look up a pixel size the driver already reports
findings.what_happened: Onboarding step 8 has a 'Camera pixel size' field whose placeholder is literally 'Look this up in your camera spec sheet', even though a camera was already chosen in step 3 and the driver reports pixel size. Step 9 then makes the user pick their camera a second time from a separate 'Camera library' to seed gain/offset. The rest of this step is excellent -- the telescope library is well stocked, and the computed values are exactly right (550 mm x 0.80 = 440.0 mm, f/4.40, 206.265 x 3.76 / 440 = 1.76 arcsec/px, all verified against the displayed numbers).
findings.expected: Prefill pixel size from the selected camera (with an override), and reuse the step-3 camera identity to seed the step-9 defaults instead of asking the user to identify their camera twice.
findings.repro: 1. Onboarding step 3: pick the camera. 2. Step 8: 'Camera pixel size' is empty with the spec-sheet placeholder. 3. Step 9: 'Choose from camera library' asks for the camera again.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-15-opticaltrain.png (empty pixel-size field), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-21-camlib.png (second camera picker), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-optics2.png (correct computed values)
findings.proposed_fix: Query the chosen camera driver (or the camera-library preset) for pixel size and prefill it, keeping the field editable.

findings.title: The capture-folder step offers no default and no way to type a path
findings.what_happened: Step 10 shows 'No folder selected yet' with a single 'Browse' button that opens the native GTK chooser. There is no suggested default (~/Pictures/Skotiq or similar) and no text field to type or paste a path -- which matters on a headless/appliance install driven over VNC or a small screen. Once chosen it does verify writability ('Folder is writable.'), which is genuinely good, and Next is correctly blocked with 'Pick a capture folder.' until one is set.
findings.expected: Prefill a sensible per-platform default that the user can accept with one click, and accept a typed/pasted path alongside Browse.
findings.repro: 1. Onboarding step 10. 2. Only 'Browse' is offered; Next is blocked until a folder is chosen.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-23-capturefolder.png, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-folder.png ('Folder is writable.')
findings.proposed_fix: Default to a platform pictures/Skotiq path, create it on accept, and add an editable path field.

findings.title: Equipment Settings mixes auto-save and Apply-required sections and repeats its own title
findings.what_happened: The gear at the top-right of the Equipment screen opens 'Equipment Settings', whose dialog title bar and first content heading both read 'Equipment Settings'. Camera Settings (gain/offset), Mount Settings (meridian flip, flip offset) and Focuser Settings (temp comp, coefficient, backlash) have no Apply and appear to save on edit, while the Built-in Guider block at the bottom has its own Reset/Apply pair plus a 'Last applied: exp 1.0s, gain 100, bin 1, cal 250ms' line. There is nothing telling the user which sections need Apply. The dialog is also short relative to the window, so the two-column masonry content scrolls in a cramped viewport with the right column running far past the left.
findings.expected: One save model per dialog. If the guider genuinely needs an explicit apply (it pushes to a running guider), say so on the section; otherwise make everything consistent.
findings.repro: 1. Equipment > gear (top right). 2. Note the duplicated 'Equipment Settings' heading. 3. Scroll: only Built-in Guider has Reset/Apply.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-47-settingstab.png (duplicate title), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-eqset3.png (Reset/Apply + 'Last applied' on the guider block only)
findings.proposed_fix: Drop the duplicated in-content heading, and either give every section an explicit Apply or annotate the guider section with why it alone needs one.

findings.title: INDI and Alpaca startup discovery default to off after the wizard offered them as scan backends
findings.what_happened: Onboarding step 2 presents Native, Alpaca and INDI as pre-checked scan backends (only Sim is off). Settings > Equipment > Connection then shows 'Query INDI on startup' and 'Query Alpaca on startup' both defaulting to OFF, with an INDI server address of localhost:7624. So a Linux user who accepts the wizard's defaults gets INDI listed as a backend but never actually queried at startup, and the two surfaces disagree about whether INDI is in play.
findings.expected: The wizard's backend selection should drive these toggles, or the toggles should default on when a server address is configured. At minimum the two screens should not contradict each other.
findings.repro: 1. Onboarding step 2: INDI and Alpaca are checked by default. 2. Finish onboarding. 3. Settings > Equipment > Connection: 'Query INDI on startup' and 'Query Alpaca on startup' are both off.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-02-drivers.png (INDI/Alpaca checked), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-conn.png (both startup queries off)
findings.proposed_fix: Persist the wizard's backend choices into the startup-query toggles.

findings.title: Discovery says only that no switches or cover calibrators were found, without saying why or what to do
findings.what_happened: For the two device classes with no simulator, the expanded Discovery panel ends with two bare italic lines, 'No cover / calibrators found' and 'No switches found', each with a refresh icon -- while every other class gets a titled section with a '1 found' count. There is no indication of which backends were searched, whether an error occurred, or how to add one manually (e.g. an Alpaca or INDI address). The app log does record 'Discovery complete for Switch: 0 devices, 0 backend errors', so the information exists.
findings.expected: Match the other sections: 'SWITCHES - 0 found', with a subtitle naming the backends scanned and a hint such as 'Switches are usually reached over Alpaca or INDI - configure a server in Settings > Connection.'
findings.repro: 1. Equipment > Discovery > Expand. 2. Scroll to the bottom of the device list.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-disc-bottom.png
findings.proposed_fix: Render zero-result classes with the same section chrome and a one-line reason plus a route to configure a remote server.

verified_correct: Onboarding driver step validation: unchecking all four backends and pressing Next is correctly blocked with 'Pick at least one driver to scan.' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-04-camera-nodrivers.png). Camera step likewise blocks with 'Pick a camera to continue, or use "Skip onboarding" to set it up later.'

Optical-train arithmetic is exactly right. I fed it 550 mm / 100 mm / 0.80x / 3.76 um and it produced effective FL 440.0 mm, f/4.40 and 1.76 arcsec/px; 206.265 x 3.76 / 440 = 1.7626, and 550/100 = 5.50 before the reducer was applied. (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-optics.png, crop-optics2.png)

Observing-site validation: latitude 95 -> 'Latitude must be between -90 and 90.' inline and in a banner; longitude 200 -> 'Longitude must be between -180 and 180.' The IP-geolocation card is unusually honest: 'This is where your internet provider appears to be, not where your telescope is, so it can be tens of kilometres out.' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-latlon.png, crop-lon.png, equipment-shell-26-site.png)

PHD2 connection test is honest: with nothing on port 4400 it reports 'No response on localhost:4400. Is PHD2 running with "Enable Server" turned on?' rather than a false success. (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-phd2.png) -- this is exactly what the INDI test should do and does not.

Onboarding Review screen matched the database field for field: camera/mount/focuser/filter wheel ids, 'Filters LumTest, R, G, B, Ha, OIII, SII', 'gain 100 - offset 50 - bin 1x1 - -10 C', capture folder, site 39.9817/-75.4072; and it honestly printed 'Guider - not set -' rather than claiming the failed PHD2 config counted. I tried to break it by renaming filter slot 1, adding and deleting a slot, and typing invalid coordinates first. (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-30-review.png + equipment_profiles row dump)
Capture folder writability check: after choosing a directory the step shows 'Folder is writable.' rather than assuming.

Disconnecting a cooled camera raises 'Disconnect cooled camera? The camera cooler is still running (sensor at -10.0 C). Disconnecting cuts cooler power abruptly - use Warm Up first for a gentle ramp to ambient.' with Cancel / 'Disconnect anyway'. Better than NINA's default behaviour. (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-camdisc2.png)

Manual cooling works end to end: 'Cool to -10C' took the simulated sensor from 20.0 C / 0% to -10.0 C / 35% in under a minute, and 'Cool on connect' (once enabled) reached -10.0 C automatically on the next Connect All.

Responsive layout down to 900px is genuinely good: Settings collapses to a single-column list with chevrons, the Equipment screen folds the profile sidebar into a 'My First Rig' dropdown sheet (Disconnect All / Edit Profile still reachable) and the status panel into accordion rows, with no horizontal overflow or clipped text anywhere I looked. I specifically checked that Connect All / Disconnect All do not become unreachable. (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-narrow.png, crop-narrow-eq.png, crop-narrow-profdd.png)
Collapsed nav rail keeps tooltips: hovering an icon-only rail item shows 'Sequencer / Automation'. (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-hover.png)
Red night theme persists correctly (app_settings.theme = 'redNight'), applies across screens, and reverts cleanly to 'dark'. Only the accent swatches escape it (reported separately).

Diagnostic dump content is truthful about what it could not collect: with no sequence loaded, sequence.json contains {"current_sequence": null, "note": "No sequence is currently loaded."} and manifest.json marks all five entries 'ok'. system_info.json reports the real app version 6.1.0 build 25 and the real Dart/OS versions. (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/diagdump.zip)

Analytics > Diagnostics tab empty state is honest and specific: 'No sessions available' plus 'Select an imaging session to analyze - Optical diagnostics require plate-solved frames with PSF and residual data.' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-102-diagtab.png)

First Light candidate cutouts are explicitly labelled 'Schematic - from measured shape, not raw pixels', and the detail screen says 'Seen once. Chase it again to build a light curve. A light curve needs at least two nights with a measured delta-mag.' The RA/Dec conversion is correct: 10.6847 deg -> 00h 42m 44.3s, 41.2687 deg -> +41 16' 7.3". The First Light header also correctly refuses to run: 'Atlas not deep enough here yet - 361 of 361 covered tiles still need more frames before differencing can run.' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-106-fl3.png, equipment-shell-107-fldetail.png)

The First Night Walkthrough's seven steps are written with real, specific, correct astrophotography content (cooler settle before autofocus, HFR V-curve fitting, PHD2 RMS thresholds of <1" excellent / 1-2" fine / >3" needs recalibration, plate-solve-and-nudge framing). Its 'Show me on the <screen>' deep-links navigate correctly. (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-fnb-4.png, crop-fnb-5.png, crop-fnb-6.png, crop-fnb-7.png)

Session-share button in the status bar correctly does nothing because remote access is not running: source shows onTap is null unless webState.isRunning, with the tooltip 'Remote access is not running'. Verified at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/widgets/status_bar/session_sharing.dart:31-35 after observing the non-response.

Profile delete Undo genuinely restores everything: after undoing the deletion of the only profile, the row returned with name, focal_length, all seven filter names, default_gain, cool_on_connect=1, is_default=1 and is_active=1 intact.
New Profile name validation: saving with an empty name is blocked with 'Fix 1 problem before saving - Profile name is required' plus an inline field error. (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-emptyname.png)

The unassigned safety monitor connected by Connect All carries an accurate caveat on its card: 'This session only - not saved to your profile, so it will not reconnect next launch. Use Assign in Discovery to keep it.'
coverage_note: Drove the real Linux release bundle on display :88 with profile 'equipment-shell' for the full session: a --fresh run through all 13 onboarding steps, then the whole Equipment surface with the nine simulated devices, three app restarts (two deliberate, one crash), a window-resize sweep, and the First Light / diagnostics / tutorial surfaces. 33 of my 36 enumerated units were reached; the three unreached ones are listed with reasons (two need hardware that does not exist on this platform, one is blocked by a defect I report). Every DEFECT below was observed live; the four highest-severity ones were cross-checked against the SQLite database or the app log rather than trusted from the screen. Screenshots are at /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-*.png with crops named crop-*.png; the checkpoint evidence is preserved at /tmp/ns-audit/shots/checkpoint-evidence.json and the diagnostic dump at /tmp/ns-audit/shots/diagdump.zip. Three caveats on my own work. (1) I could not reach the Science screen (/science) from the desktop nav at all -- it has no rail entry and every caller (science HUD chip, cockpit narrator, sequencer panels) needs frames with science data; I reached First Light instead through Analytics > Science > First Light, and I had to seed one row into transient_detections to make the candidate card render, so the card and detail screen were exercised with synthetic data. My first seed used a non-integer tile_id which produced a raw FormatException in the UI; that specific exception is my fault and I do not report it, but the dead Retry button it exposed is real and reproducible. (2) The app process died once while I was bisecting the responsive breakpoint (log ends 'Timed out waiting for OpenGL frame of size 860x700 (have 760x700)'). I judge that a softpipe artifact of repeated rapid resizes under the audit harness, not a product defect, so I have not reported it -- but it is worth one check on real hardware. (3) The harness's `shot` command changed mid-run to crop-and-downscale to 1280px; screenshots before roughly equipment-shell-93 are full-root 1920x1200 and later ones are 1280x720 window crops, so click coordinates in my repro steps are screen-absolute throughout. I stopped the app and its Xvfb at the end.
